terms.name: AAA (Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting)
terms.definition: Security framework that verifies who you are, what you can access, and logs what you did on a network or system.

terms.name: ACL (Access Control List)
terms.definition: Ruleset that specifies which users or systems are allowed or denied access to a resource such as a file, folder, or network.

terms.name: ADF (Automatic Document Feeder)
terms.definition: Printer/scanner tray that feeds multipage documents automatically so you do not have to place each sheet on the glass.

terms.name: AES (Advanced Encryption Standard)
terms.definition: Widely used symmetric encryption algorithm that protects data at rest and in transit with strong, standardized ciphers.

terms.name: AMD (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.)
terms.definition: CPU and GPU manufacturer whose processors and graphics chips compete with Intel and NVIDIA in PCs and servers.

terms.name: AP (Access Point)
terms.definition: Wireless network device that lets Wi-Fi clients connect to a wired LAN or the internet.

terms.name: APFS (Apple File System)
terms.definition: Modern Apple disk file system optimized for SSDs, with strong encryption, snapshots, and space sharing on macOS and iOS.

terms.name: APIPA (Automatic Private Internet Protocol Addressing)
terms.definition: Windows feature that assigns a 169.254.x.x address when DHCP fails so the host can still talk on the local link.

terms.name: ARM (Advanced RISC (Reduced Instruction Set Computer) Machine)
terms.definition: CPU architecture used in phones, tablets, and many laptops that emphasizes efficiency with a reduced instruction set.

terms.name: ATX (Advanced Technology Extended)
terms.definition: Common PC motherboard and power-supply form factor that defines board size, mounting holes, and connector layout.

terms.name: AUP (Acceptable Use Policy)
terms.definition: Organizational rules describing allowed and prohibited uses of company computers, networks, and internet access.

terms.name: BEC (Business Email Compromise)
terms.definition: Social-engineering fraud where attackers impersonate executives or vendors by email to steal money or data.

terms.name: BIOS (Basic Input/Output System)
terms.definition: Legacy firmware that initializes hardware at power-on and starts the boot process before the OS loads.

terms.name: BNC (Bayonet Neill-Concelman)
terms.definition: Coaxial connector with a twist-lock bayonet coupling, historically used on older network and video cabling.

terms.name: BSOD (Blue Screen of Death)
terms.definition: Windows stop-error screen shown when the OS encounters a critical fault it cannot recover from safely.

terms.name: BYOD (Bring Your Own Device)
terms.definition: Policy that lets employees use personal phones or laptops for work, usually managed with MDM and security controls.

terms.name: CAC (Calling-card Authorization Computer)
terms.definition: Smart-card style credential used to authenticate users for secure access in government and enterprise environments.

terms.name: CAS (Column Address Strobe)
terms.definition: Memory timing signal related to how DRAM columns are addressed; often discussed with RAM latency (CAS latency).

terms.name: CIFS (Common Internet File System)
terms.definition: Microsoft file-sharing dialect of SMB that lets clients access networked files and printers over TCP/IP.

terms.name: CMDB (Configuration Management Database)
terms.definition: Central inventory of IT assets and their relationships used for change, incident, and asset management.

terms.name: CMOS (Complementary Metal-Oxide Semiconductor)
terms.definition: Low-power chip technology; in PCs it often refers to the battery-backed chip storing BIOS/UEFI settings.

terms.name: CNAME (Canonical Name)
terms.definition: DNS record that aliases one hostname to another canonical hostname.

terms.name: CPU (Central Processing Unit)
terms.definition: Primary processor that executes program instructions and performs most computing work in a device.

terms.name: DB-9 (Serial Communications D-Shell Connector, 9 pins)
terms.definition: Nine-pin D-sub serial connector historically used for RS-232 devices, consoles, and older peripherals.

terms.name: DDoS (Distributed Denial of Service)
terms.definition: Attack that floods a target from many compromised systems to overwhelm availability of a service.

terms.name: DDR (Double Data Rate)
terms.definition: Memory technology that transfers data on both clock edges, used in successive generations of RAM modules.

terms.name: DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol)
terms.definition: Network service that automatically assigns IP addresses and related settings to clients.

terms.name: DIMM (Dual In-line Memory Module)
terms.definition: Standard stick form factor for desktop and server RAM with contacts on both sides of the module.

terms.name: DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail)
terms.definition: Email authentication method that signs outbound messages so receivers can verify the sending domain.

terms.name: DLP (Data Loss Prevention)
terms.definition: Security controls that detect and block unauthorized transfer or leakage of sensitive data.

terms.name: DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance)
terms.definition: Email policy framework that builds on SPF/DKIM and tells receivers how to handle failed authentication.

terms.name: DNS (Domain Name System)
terms.definition: Internet directory that resolves human-readable names to IP addresses and related records.

terms.name: DoS (Denial of Service)
terms.definition: Attack that makes a system or network unavailable by exhausting resources or crashing a service.

terms.name: DRM (Digital Rights Management)
terms.definition: Technology that restricts how digital media or software can be copied, shared, or used.

terms.name: DSL (Digital Subscriber Line)
terms.definition: Broadband internet technology that delivers data over telephone copper lines.

terms.name: DVI (Digital Visual Interface)
terms.definition: Video connector standard used to link computers to monitors, supporting digital (and sometimes analog) signals.

terms.name: ECC (Error-correcting Code)
terms.definition: Memory feature that detects and corrects bit errors, common in servers for higher reliability.

terms.name: EDR (Endpoint Detection and Response)
terms.definition: Security platform that monitors endpoints for threats and supports investigation and remediation.

terms.name: EFS (Encrypting File System)
terms.definition: Windows feature that encrypts individual files and folders with user-tied keys.

terms.name: EOL (End-of-life)
terms.definition: Point when a product no longer receives updates or vendor support and should be replaced or mitigated.

terms.name: eSATA (External Serial Advanced Technology Attachment)
terms.definition: External SATA interface for connecting outside hard drives at SATA speeds.

terms.name: ESD (Electrostatic Discharge)
terms.definition: Sudden static electricity surge that can damage sensitive electronic components during handling.

terms.name: eSIM (Embedded SIM)
terms.definition: Software-based SIM built into a device that can be provisioned without a physical SIM card.

terms.name: EULA (End-user License Agreement)
terms.definition: Legal contract defining the terms under which a user may install and use software.

terms.name: exFAT (Extended File Allocation Table)
terms.definition: Microsoft file system designed for flash media with large file support across Windows, macOS, and more.

terms.name: FaaS (Function As A Service)
terms.definition: Cloud model that runs event-triggered code functions without managing servers (serverless).

terms.name: FAT32 (32-bit File Allocation Table)
terms.definition: Older widely compatible file system with a 4 GB per-file size limit, still used on USB drives.

terms.name: FRT (Facial Recognition Technology)
terms.definition: Biometric method that identifies or unlocks devices by analyzing facial features.

terms.name: FTP (File Transfer Protocol)
terms.definition: Classic protocol for uploading and downloading files; often replaced by SFTP for security.

terms.name: GFS (Grandfather-Father-Son)
terms.definition: Backup rotation scheme that keeps daily, weekly, and monthly copies on a staggered schedule.

terms.name: GPS (Global Positioning System)
terms.definition: Satellite navigation system that provides location and time data to GPS receivers.

terms.name: GPT (GUID (Globally Unique Identifier) Partition Table)
terms.definition: Modern disk partitioning scheme that supports large disks and many partitions, replacing MBR limits.

terms.name: GPU (Graphics Processing Unit)
terms.definition: Processor specialized for rendering graphics and accelerating parallel workloads like video and AI.

terms.name: GUI (Graphical User Interface)
terms.definition: Visual interface of windows, icons, and menus that users interact with instead of pure text commands.

terms.name: GUID (Globally Unique Identifier)
terms.definition: 128-bit unique ID used to identify software objects, partitions, and other entities without collision.

terms.name: HD (High Definition)
terms.definition: Video quality standard with higher resolution than standard definition (commonly 720p or 1080p).

terms.name: HDD (Hard Disk Drive)
terms.definition: Magnetic spinning-disk storage device used for bulk data storage at lower cost per gigabyte.

terms.name: HDMI (High-definition Media Interface)
terms.definition: Digital audio/video connector that carries uncompressed video and multi-channel audio to displays.

terms.name: HSM (Hardware Security Module)
terms.definition: Tamper-resistant device that generates and stores cryptographic keys for high-security operations.

terms.name: HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol)
terms.definition: Application protocol that transfers web pages and API data between browsers and servers (unencrypted).

terms.name: HTTPS (Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure)
terms.definition: HTTP wrapped in TLS encryption to protect web traffic confidentiality and integrity.

terms.name: IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service)
terms.definition: Cloud model that rents virtual servers, storage, and networking for customers to configure.

terms.name: IAM (Identity Access Management)
terms.definition: Policies and tools that control user identities, authentication, and access rights across systems.

terms.name: IMAP (Internet Mail Access Protocol)
terms.definition: Email protocol that keeps messages on the server and syncs mailboxes across multiple devices.

terms.name: IOPS (Input/Output Operations Per Second)
terms.definition: Performance metric measuring how many read/write operations a storage device can handle per second.

terms.name: IoT (Internet of Things)
terms.definition: Network of everyday devices (sensors, appliances, cameras) connected to the internet for data and control.

terms.name: IP (Internet Protocol)
terms.definition: Core network protocol that addresses and routes packets between hosts on an IP network.

terms.name: IPS (In-plane Switching)
terms.definition: LCD panel technology known for wide viewing angles and accurate colors compared with TN panels.

terms.name: IR (Infrared)
terms.definition: Wireless line-of-sight communication or sensing using infrared light, used in remotes and some sensors.

terms.name: ISO (International Organization for Standardization)
terms.definition: Standards body; also casually used for disk image files (.iso) that mirror optical media.

terms.name: ISP (Internet Service Provider)
terms.definition: Company that provides customers with internet connectivity and related services.

terms.name: ITX (Information Technology eXtended)
terms.definition: Smaller motherboard form-factor family (such as Mini-ITX) for compact PCs.

terms.name: KVM (Keyboard-Video-Mouse)
terms.definition: Switch or device that lets one keyboard, mouse, and monitor control multiple computers.

terms.name: LAN (Local Area Network)
terms.definition: Network covering a limited area such as a home, office, or building.

terms.name: LC (Lucent Connector)
terms.definition: Small form-factor fiber-optic connector commonly used in high-density network installations.

terms.name: LCD (Liquid Crystal Display)
terms.definition: Flat-panel display technology that uses liquid crystals and a backlight to form images.

terms.name: LDAP (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol)
terms.definition: Protocol for querying and managing directory services such as user accounts and groups.

terms.name: LED (Light-emitting Diode)
terms.definition: Semiconductor light source used for indicators, lighting, and modern display backlights.

terms.name: LTE (Long-Term Evolution)
terms.definition: High-speed cellular wireless standard commonly known as 4G LTE mobile data.

terms.name: MAC (Media Access Control)
terms.definition: Hardware address uniquely identifying a network interface on a local network segment.

terms.name: MAN (Metropolitan Area Network)
terms.definition: Network spanning a city or campus, larger than a LAN but smaller than a WAN.

terms.name: MBR (Master Boot Record)
terms.definition: Legacy disk boot sector and partitioning scheme limited to four primary partitions and 2 TB disks.

terms.name: MDM (Mobile Device Management)
terms.definition: Enterprise software that configures, secures, and remotely manages smartphones and tablets.

terms.name: MDR (Managed Detection and Response)
terms.definition: Outsourced security service that monitors for threats and helps respond to incidents.

terms.name: MFA (Multifactor Authentication)
terms.definition: Login requirement that combines two or more factors (something you know, have, or are).

terms.name: MFP (Multifunction Printer)
terms.definition: Office device that combines printing, scanning, copying, and often faxing in one unit.

terms.name: MMC (Microsoft Management Console)
terms.definition: Windows shell that hosts administrative snap-ins such as Device Manager and Event Viewer tools.

terms.name: MNDA (Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement)
terms.definition: Contract where both parties agree to keep shared confidential information secret.

terms.name: mSATA (Mini-serial Advanced Technology Attachment)
terms.definition: Compact SATA connector/form factor used for small SSDs in laptops and embedded systems.

terms.name: MX (Mail Exchange)
terms.definition: DNS record that tells senders which mail servers accept email for a domain.

terms.name: NAC (Network Access Control)
terms.definition: Security approach that authenticates and checks devices before granting network access.

terms.name: NAS (Network Access Server)
terms.definition: Device or service that authenticates remote users and grants them access to network resources.

terms.name: NAT (Network Address Translation)
terms.definition: Router technique that maps private internal IPs to public addresses for internet access.

terms.name: NDA (Non-Disclosure Agreement)
terms.definition: Legal contract requiring one or more parties not to reveal confidential information.

terms.name: NetBIOS (Network Basic Input/Output System)
terms.definition: Legacy Windows networking API/name service used historically for local name resolution and shares.

terms.name: NFC (Near-field Communication)
terms.definition: Short-range wireless tech for payments, pairing, and data exchange within a few centimeters.

terms.name: NIC (Network Interface Card)
terms.definition: Hardware adapter that connects a computer to a wired or wireless network.

terms.name: NTFS (New Technology File System)
terms.definition: Default Windows file system supporting permissions, encryption, compression, and large volumes.

terms.name: NTP (Network Time Protocol)
terms.definition: Protocol that synchronizes device clocks with authoritative time servers.

terms.name: NVMe (Non-volatile Memory Express)
terms.definition: High-speed SSD interface protocol designed for PCIe flash storage with low latency.

terms.name: OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer)
terms.definition: Company that builds hardware or software sold under another brand or bundled with systems.

terms.name: OLED (Organic Light-emitting Diode)
terms.definition: Display technology where each pixel emits its own light, enabling deep blacks and high contrast.

terms.name: ONT (Optical Network Terminal)
terms.definition: Fiber-to-the-premises device that converts optical signals to Ethernet for home or business use.

terms.name: OS (Operating System)
terms.definition: Core software that manages hardware, processes, memory, and provides services for applications.

terms.name: OTP (One-time Password/Passcode)
terms.definition: Single-use code used for authentication, often delivered by app, SMS, or hardware token.

terms.name: PaaS (Platform as a Service)
terms.definition: Cloud model that provides a managed runtime platform so developers deploy apps without managing OS infrastructure.

terms.name: PAM (Privileged Access Management)
terms.definition: Controls that secure, monitor, and limit use of powerful admin accounts and credentials.

terms.name: PAN (Personal Area Network)
terms.definition: Very short-range network around a person, such as Bluetooth between phone and headset.

terms.name: PC (Personal Computer)
terms.definition: General-purpose computer designed for individual use, such as a desktop or laptop.

terms.name: PCI (Peripheral Component Interconnect)
terms.definition: Older parallel expansion-bus standard for adding cards to a motherboard.

terms.name: PCIe (Peripheral Component Interconnect Express)
terms.definition: Modern high-speed serial expansion bus used for GPUs, NVMe SSDs, and add-in cards.

terms.name: PCL (Printer Command Language)
terms.definition: HP page-description language that tells printers how to render text and graphics.

terms.name: PII (Personally Identifiable Information)
terms.definition: Data that can identify an individual, such as name, SSN, or email, requiring careful protection.

terms.name: PIN (Personal Identification Number)
terms.definition: Numeric secret used to authenticate a user, often with a card, phone unlock, or smart card.

terms.name: PIV (Personal Identity Verification)
terms.definition: U.S. federal smart-card standard for employee identity and strong authentication.

terms.name: PoE (Power over Ethernet)
terms.definition: Technology that delivers electrical power and data over the same Ethernet cable to devices like APs and cameras.

terms.name: POP (Post Office Protocol)
terms.definition: Email retrieval protocol that typically downloads messages to a client and may remove them from the server.

terms.name: POST (Power-on Self-test)
terms.definition: Firmware diagnostic sequence that checks critical hardware before the OS boots.

terms.name: PSU (Power Supply Unit)
terms.definition: Component that converts wall AC power into the DC voltages a computer needs.

terms.name: PUP (Potentially Unwanted Program)
terms.definition: Software that is not outright malware but is undesirable (adware, toolbars, bundled junk).

terms.name: PXE (Preboot eXecution Environment)
terms.definition: Network boot technology that lets a PC load an OS installer or image from a server.

terms.name: QoS (Quality of Service)
terms.definition: Networking techniques that prioritize certain traffic (voice, video) for better performance.

terms.name: RADIUS (Remote Authentication Dial-in User Server)
terms.definition: Centralized AAA protocol commonly used for VPN, Wi-Fi, and network device authentication.

terms.name: RAID (Redundant Array of Independent Disks)
terms.definition: Disk configuration that combines drives for performance, capacity, and/or fault tolerance.

terms.name: RAM (Random-access Memory)
terms.definition: Volatile working memory the CPU uses to store running programs and data.

terms.name: RDP (Remote Desktop Protocol)
terms.definition: Microsoft protocol that provides remote graphical desktop access to Windows systems.

terms.name: ReFS (Resilient File System)
terms.definition: Microsoft file system focused on integrity and resilience for large volumes and storage spaces.

terms.name: RFID (Radio-frequency Identification)
terms.definition: Wireless ID technology using tags and readers for access control, inventory, and tracking.

terms.name: RGB (Red-Green-Blue)
terms.definition: Additive color model used by displays and lighting where colors are mixed from red, green, and blue.

terms.name: RISC (Reduced Instruction Set Computer)
terms.definition: CPU design philosophy using a smaller, simpler instruction set for efficiency (as in ARM).

terms.name: RJ11 (Registered Jack Function 11)
terms.definition: Telephone connector typically used for landline/DSL with fewer contacts than RJ45.

terms.name: RJ45 (Registered Jack Function 45)
terms.definition: Eight-position modular connector used for Ethernet networking cables.

terms.name: RMM (Remote Monitoring and Management)
terms.definition: MSP platform used to monitor, patch, and manage many client endpoints from one console.

terms.name: RPM (Revolutions Per Minute)
terms.definition: Speed measurement for spinning devices such as HDD platters or cooling fans.

terms.name: RSR (Rapid Security Response)
terms.definition: Fast security update mechanism (notably Apple) that delivers urgent fixes outside major OS releases.

terms.name: SaaS (Software as a Service)
terms.definition: Cloud model delivering applications over the internet (e.g., Microsoft 365, Google Workspace).

terms.name: SAML (Security Assertions Markup Language)
terms.definition: XML-based standard for exchanging authentication/authorization data, often used for SSO.

terms.name: SAN (Storage Area Network)
terms.definition: High-speed dedicated network that provides block-level storage to servers.

terms.name: SAS (Serial Attached SCSI (Small Computer System Interface))
terms.definition: Enterprise disk interface that connects servers to high-reliability SAS drives.

terms.name: SATA (Serial Advanced Technology Attachment)
terms.definition: Common interface for connecting internal HDDs and SSDs to a motherboard.

terms.name: SC (Subscriber Connector)
terms.definition: Square push-pull fiber-optic connector used in networking and telecom.

terms.name: SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition)
terms.definition: Industrial control system used to monitor and operate infrastructure like plants and utilities.

terms.name: SCSI (Small Computer System Interface)
terms.definition: Legacy/enterprise peripheral interface for disks and other devices; ancestor concepts live on in SAS.

terms.name: SD (Secure Digital)
terms.definition: Removable flash memory card format used in cameras, phones, and embedded devices.

terms.name: SDS (Safety Data Sheet)
terms.definition: Document listing hazards, handling, and disposal guidance for a chemical or material (formerly MSDS).

terms.name: SFTP (Secure File Transfer Protocol)
terms.definition: Encrypted file transfer method that runs over SSH instead of plaintext FTP.

terms.name: SIM (Subscriber Identity Module)
terms.definition: Card that stores mobile subscriber identity and authentication data for cellular service.

terms.name: SLA (Service-level Agreement)
terms.definition: Contract defining expected service performance, uptime, and response times between provider and customer.

terms.name: S.M.A.R.T (Self-monitoring Analysis and Reporting Technology)
terms.definition: Drive self-diagnostics that report health metrics to warn of impending disk failure.

terms.name: SMB (Server Message Block)
terms.definition: Windows file-and-printer sharing protocol used for networked resources.

terms.name: SMS (Short Message Service)
terms.definition: Cellular text messaging service used for communication and sometimes OTP delivery.

terms.name: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol)
terms.definition: Protocol that sends email between mail clients and mail servers.

terms.name: SNMP (Simple Network Management Protocol)
terms.definition: Protocol for monitoring and managing network devices such as switches, routers, and printers.

terms.name: SODIMM (Small Outline Dual In-line Memory Module)
terms.definition: Compact RAM module form factor used in laptops and small-form-factor systems.

terms.name: SOHO (Small Office/Home Office)
terms.definition: Small business/home work environment with simpler networking and fewer users than enterprise.

terms.name: SOP (Standard Operating Procedure)
terms.definition: Documented step-by-step process for performing a routine IT or business task consistently.

terms.name: SPF (Sender Policy Framework)
terms.definition: Email DNS record that lists servers authorized to send mail for a domain.

terms.name: SPICE (Simple Protocol for Independent Computing Environments)
terms.definition: Remote-display protocol optimized for accessing virtual machines with graphics and clipboard sharing.

terms.name: SQL (Structured Query Language)
terms.definition: Standard language for querying and managing relational databases.

terms.name: SSD (Solid-state Drive)
terms.definition: Flash-based storage with no moving parts, offering higher speed and durability than HDDs.

terms.name: SSH (Secure Shell)
terms.definition: Encrypted remote command-line protocol that replaced insecure Telnet for administration.

terms.name: SSID (Service Set Identifier)
terms.definition: Human-readable name of a Wi-Fi network that clients see when scanning for wireless networks.

terms.name: SSO (Single Sign-on)
terms.definition: Authentication approach where one login grants access to multiple related applications.

terms.name: ST (Straight Tip)
terms.definition: Bayonet-style fiber-optic connector with a round ferrule, used in older fiber installations.

terms.name: TACACS (Terminal Access Controller Access-control System)
terms.definition: Cisco-oriented AAA protocol for authenticating administrators to network devices.

terms.name: TCP (Transmission Control Protocol)
terms.definition: Reliable, connection-oriented transport protocol that delivers ordered, acknowledged data streams.

terms.name: TKIP (Temporal Key Integrity Protocol)
terms.definition: Legacy WPA encryption/integrity mechanism superseded by stronger AES-based Wi-Fi security.

terms.name: TN (Twisted Nematic)
terms.definition: Fast, inexpensive LCD panel type with narrower viewing angles than IPS or VA.

terms.name: TOTP (Time-based One-time Password)
terms.definition: OTP algorithm that generates rotating codes based on the current time and a shared secret.

terms.name: TPM (Trusted Platform Module)
terms.definition: Secure cryptoprocessor chip that stores keys and supports features like BitLocker and measured boot.

terms.name: TXT (Text)
terms.definition: DNS record type that stores arbitrary text, often used for SPF, DKIM, and domain verification.

terms.name: UAC (User Account Control)
terms.definition: Windows security prompt that asks for elevation before allowing administrative actions.

terms.name: UDP (User Datagram Protocol)
terms.definition: Connectionless transport protocol used for fast, lightweight traffic such as DNS and streaming.

terms.name: UEFI (Unified Extensible Firmware Interface)
terms.definition: Modern firmware interface that replaces legacy BIOS with faster boot, GUI setup, and Secure Boot.

terms.name: UPnP (Universal Plug and Play)
terms.definition: Protocol that lets devices automatically open router ports; convenient but often a security risk.

terms.name: UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply)
terms.definition: Battery-backed power device that keeps equipment running during outages and smooths power issues.

terms.name: USB (Universal Serial Bus)
terms.definition: Hot-pluggable interface for connecting peripherals, storage, and chargers to computers.

terms.name: USB-C (Universal Serial Bus Type C)
terms.definition: Reversible USB connector supporting data, video, and high-wattage power delivery.

terms.name: UTM (Unified Threat Management)
terms.definition: Security appliance that combines firewall, IDS/IPS, antivirus, and related protections in one box.

terms.name: VA (Vertical Alignment)
terms.definition: LCD panel technology with strong contrast, sitting between TN and IPS in viewing-angle performance.

terms.name: VDI (Virtual Desktop Infrastructure)
terms.definition: Architecture that hosts user desktops as VMs in a data center and streams them to thin clients.

terms.name: VGA (Video Graphics Array)
terms.definition: Legacy analog video connector and resolution standard historically used for PC monitors.

terms.name: VLAN (Virtual LAN (Local Area Network))
terms.definition: Logical network segment created on switches to isolate broadcast domains without separate physical cabling.

terms.name: VM (Virtual Machine)
terms.definition: Software-emulated computer running an OS and apps on a hypervisor alongside other VMs.

terms.name: VNC (Virtual Network Computer)
terms.definition: Cross-platform remote desktop technology that shares a graphical desktop over the RFB protocol.

terms.name: VoIP (Voice over Internet Protocol)
terms.definition: Technology that carries voice calls as data packets over IP networks instead of traditional phone lines.

terms.name: VPN (Virtual Private Network)
terms.definition: Encrypted tunnel that securely connects a remote client or site to a private network over the internet.

terms.name: VRAM (Video Random-access Memory)
terms.definition: Memory used by a GPU to store textures, framebuffers, and other graphics data.

terms.name: WAN (Wide Area Network)
terms.definition: Network spanning large geographic areas, typically connecting multiple sites over ISP links.

terms.name: WAP (Wireless Access Point)
terms.definition: Device that bridges wireless clients onto a wired network (often used interchangeably with AP).

terms.name: WEP (Wired Equivalent Privacy)
terms.definition: Obsolete Wi-Fi security protocol that is easily cracked and must not be used.

terms.name: WinRM (Windows Remote Management)
terms.definition: Microsoft service that enables remote PowerShell and management commands without a full desktop session.

terms.name: WISP (Written Internet Service Provider)
terms.definition: Provider of internet service (exam acronym expansion); in practice often refers to wireless ISPs serving rural areas.

terms.name: WLAN (Wireless LAN (Local Area Network))
terms.definition: Local network that uses Wi-Fi radio instead of (or in addition to) Ethernet cabling.

terms.name: WPA (Wi-Fi Protected Access)
terms.definition: Family of Wi-Fi security standards (WPA/WPA2/WPA3) that encrypt and authenticate wireless traffic.

terms.name: WWAN (Wireless Wide Area Network)
terms.definition: Wide-area wireless connectivity such as cellular (LTE/5G) for mobile internet access.

terms.name: XaaS (Anything As A Service)
terms.definition: Broad term for delivering almost any IT capability as a cloud subscription service.

terms.name: XDR (Extended Detection and Response)
terms.definition: Security approach that correlates threat data across endpoints, email, cloud, and network for detection.

terms.name: XFS (Extended File System)
terms.definition: High-performance journaling file system commonly used on Linux for large volumes.

terms.name: XSS (Cross-site Scripting)
terms.definition: Web attack that injects malicious scripts into pages viewed by other users to steal data or hijack sessions.
